Title: Diagnosis

Details: The bug report explains a problem with `JXPathContext.iteratePointers()` when iterating over XML elements that share the same namespace URI but have different prefixes. The behavior observed is that the first element with the namespace is returned repeatedly, while other elements with different prefixes but the same namespace URI are omitted.

The failure in the test `testIterateDOM()` indicates that the issue arises when using a DOM model to iterate over elements using XPath pointers.

From the signature of the abstract method `iteratePointers(String xpath)` in `JXPathContext` (line 792), it is clear the actual implementation used during the test is critical, but we do not have it here.

Examining the class `QName` shows how qualified names are constructed with a prefix and local name. The `QName` class constructs the qualified name string using the prefix, which implies that if two prefixes point to the same namespace URI, the QName instances will differ by prefix. This difference may cause problems if namespace resolution does not properly map multiple prefixes to the same namespace URI.

Looking into `DOMNodePointer.getNamespaceResolver()`, a `NamespaceResolver` is being created and cached locally. This resolver is crucial for mapping prefixes to namespace URIs and vice versa. The bug report and a recent related issue suggest there was a regression caused by changes to `NamespaceResolver` which broke existing test cases by removing or altering reverse mapping cache behavior. This cache might be a critical piece for supporting multiple prefixes for the same namespace URI.

The key cause of the bug is likely due to the `NamespaceResolver` or its use in the XPath pointer iteration process not correctly handling multiple prefixes mapped to the same namespace URI. As a result, the iteration based on pointers using prefixes in the XPath expression returns duplicate nodes for the first prefix and completely omits nodes under other prefixes, despite the underlying namespace being the same.

The test failure in `testIterateDOM()` reveals this problem practically, where two elements have the same namespace but different prefixes and iteration incorrectly returns only one set of elements.

In summary, the issue originated because `JXPathContext.iteratePointers()` relies on namespace resolution that does not correctly handle multiple prefixes for a single namespace URI. This causes the pointer iteration mechanism to fail in distinguishing nodes by prefix in the same namespace, resulting in duplicate and missing elements when iterating.

This diagnosis aligns with both the current bug report's example and symptoms and the known issues around `NamespaceResolver` changes. The root cause is in `NamespaceResolver` or its interaction with pointer iteration logic in DOM node pointers or XPath context.

Potential places to fix this include `NamespaceResolver` logic for namespace-to-prefix mappings and the method implementing pointer iteration in `JXPathContext` or its DOM model subclass to correctly account for multiple prefixes in the same namespace.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
